mechanism: The import price index measures the dollar cost of imported goods; rising import-price growth signals imported inflation and cost pressure that can tighten financial conditions and weigh on equity valuations, while low or falling import-price growth is supportive.
key_finding: As known at the time (real-time IR vintages), the rule selected on in-sample data uses yoy at L4 (IS Sharpe 1.33) with held-out OOS Sharpe 0.83 versus buy-and-hold 1.00.
caveats: ALFRED holds import-price vintages only from 2010-03, so the as-known-at-the-time training window is short (2010 to 2016); the as-revised-today result uses the full history and is shown for comparison.
The strategy is search-selected and needs fresh holdout validation.
Import prices move with oil and the dollar; the 2008-09 collapse and the 2021-22 spike dominate the growth series.
The previous rule (20261016) was the single highest in-sample Sharpe on revised data with fixed lags; it is replaced here.
narrative_summary: Import-price growth is tested as a countercyclical inflation / cost overlay for SPY.
